source.section: TC-40 lines 4 to 22 (Instructions PDF p.9 Line 4; PDF p.10 Lines 5 to 20 and the Line 17 table; PDF p.11 Line 22)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 17,000.00 = 17,000.00. Federal taxable income = 17,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 1,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Utah starts from federal AGI). TC-40 (single): line 4 federal AGI 17,000.00. Line 5 additions: none, 0.00. Line 6 = 17,000.00 + 0.00 = 17,000.00. Line 7 state tax refund 0.00. Line 8 subtractions 0.00. Line 9 Utah taxable income = 17,000.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 17,000.00. Line 10 = 17,000.00 x 0.045 = 765.00. Lines 11 to 16, by the projection: no dependents; the deduction on line 12 is held as the cap 15,750.00; initial credit = 0.06 x min(line 9 17,000.00, cap 15,750.00) = 0.06 x 15,750.00 = 945.00. Line 17 base phase-out amount 18,213.00. Line 18 = max(0, 17,000.00 - 18,213.00) = 0.00. Line 19 = 0.00 x 0.013 = 0.000. Line 20 = max(0, 945.00 - 0.000) = 945.000. Line 21 worksheet: line 1 federal AGI 17,000.00; line 2 standard deduction 15,750.00; line 3 senior deduction 0.00 (no amount in Utah's sources); line 4 15,750.00; line 5 = max(0, 17,000.00 - 15,750.00) = 1,250.00. Line 5 is above zero, so not exempt; line 21 blank. Line 22 and TC-40A Part 3: line 20 945.000 = 945.000, limited to the tax 765.00 (nonrefundable, PDF p.11 Line 24), so credits are 765.00. relief_amounts gives each credit's worksheet figure before that limit. Tax = 765.00 - 765.00 = 0.00. Pins the cap above it: income 17,000.00 is over the cap and under the base amount, so the credit is 0.06 x 15,750.00 = 945.00, not 0.06 x 17,000.00 = 1,020.00.
